headline: Sixty Seven Swings, One Hundred And Nine Dollars Buried
paragraphs: Sixty two games graded for real, twenty passed on, forty two deemed actionable, and sixty seven plays sent out at ten dollars each. The ledger came back 27-38-2 for a loss of 108.93 on 670 staked, an ROI of negative 16.3 percent. The model expected to win 59 percent of these. It won 41.5 percent. That gap is not variance wearing a disguise, that is a faceplant with timestamps.

The moneylines were the knife: 5-11, down 38.91, with the model projecting a 49.4 percent clip and delivering 31.2. It loved Massachusetts at +230 by a full 14 probability points, which is the largest edge it claimed all week, and Buffalo won 25-18. It also had Pittsburgh at 82 percent and minus 225 before Boston College won 27-21. Spreads lost 51.83 across 32 tries. Totals were the merciful ones at 9-10.

Credit where it exists. Charlotte at Temple went over 46 in a 38-31 game the model had flagged by 8.9 points at 74 percent, and the Kentucky moneyline at +215 returned 21.50 in a 21-13 Oklahoma loss. Then the published top five went 1-4 for negative 30.91, an ROI of negative 61.8, which is the five it actually told people about. Four weeks in, the season reads 120-141-6 and minus 221.27.
